Q1.answer:
(a) The final rule is Reduction in Force, FR Doc. 2026-15665, 91 FR 49178-49227, published August 3, 2026, effective September 2, 2026, Docket OPM-2025-0107, RIN 3206-AO86.
(b) The proposed rule it finalized is Reduction in Force, FR Doc. 2026-04377, 91 FR 10904-10934, published March 5, 2026.
(c) Two corrections through today: 2026-17335, 91 FR 54794-54796, published August 25, 2026, effective September 2, 2026, correcting typographical and clerical errors in amendatory instructions and regulatory text (including part 316 cross-references, list structure in 330.202 and 351.702(a)(4)(iv), and the part 351 authority citation). 2026-18800, 91 FR 58363-58364, published and effective September 15, 2026, restoring 5 CFR 330.602(1)(i) and (ii) to the CTAP definition of displaced after amendatory instruction 11 inadvertently removed them.
(d) The amended rules govern a RIF for which the agency issues the specific RIF notice on or after September 2, 2026. A RIF for which the notice was issued before September 2, 2026 remains under the regulations in effect when the notice was issued. Stated in the DATES paragraph at 91 FR 49178 and repeated at 91 FR 49206-49207.
(e) Other 2026 final rules amending 5 CFR part 351 with effect on or after September 2, 2026: 2026-15666, Reduction in Force Appeals, 91 FR 49230, effective September 2, 2026, revising 351.802(a)(6), 351.807(e), and replacing subpart I; in force today. 2026-21316, Managing Senior Professional Performance, 91 FR 65904, effective November 18, 2026, revising 351.203 (Rating of record) and 351.503(a)(1), (b)(2), (b)(3); not in force today. 2026-21320, Administrative Leave for Workforce Realignment and Other Purposes, 91 FR 65924, effective November 18, 2026, revising 351.806 and the part 351 authority citation; not in force today. Q1.uncertainty: The correction 2026-17335 carries Docket ID OPM-2026-0107 rather than the main rule's OPM-2025-0107, as published. The full pre-September 2, 2026 text of 5 CFR 351.504 is not printed; only the amendments are.

Q2.answer:
(a) Under 5 CFR 351.503 and 351.504 as revised:
Abbott: Level 5 + Level 4 + Level 4 = 7 + 5 + 5 = 17; no preference = 0; total 17; tenure subgroup I.
Bianchi: Level 4 + Level 2 + Level 3 = 5 + 0 + 3 = 8; preference eligible with 30%+ compensable disability = +5 (AD); total 13; subgroup I.
Castillo: 7 + 5 + 5 = 17. He retired after 22 years with retired pay based on length of service, no disability. Under 351.504(b), a retired member is a preference eligible only if (b)(1), (2), or (3) applies, subject to (b)(4)-(5). His retirement is not disability-based; his retired pay is based on 20+ years; no continuous civilian employment since 1964; he is not a disabled veteran. He is not a preference eligible: 0 points, subgroup B; total 17.
Dalton: two ratings, Level 5 and Level 2. 7 + 0 = 7; proxy = 7 / 2 = 3.5; credit = 7 + 0 + 3.5 = 10.5; preference eligible no disability = +3 (A); total 13.5; subgroup I.
Eze: three Level 4 ratings = 5 + 5 + 5 = 15; no preference = 0; total 15. A four-year term is not excluded by 351.202(d)(2)(iii), which covers only temporary appointments of one year or less under part 316, subpart D; he completed the applicable probation/trial period and is in competitive service tenure subgroup II under 351.502(a)(3).
Fontaine: one rating, Level 4 = 5 x 3 = 15; no preference = 0; total 15; subgroup I.
(b) Order of retention: Abbott (17), Castillo (17), Fontaine (15), Eze (15), Dalton (13.5), Bianchi (13). Released: Dalton and Bianchi. Abbott and Castillo tie at 17 and are both in subgroup I; Abbott's SCD of May 1, 2003 is earlier than Castillo's August 1, 2012, so Abbott ranks first under 351.501(c). Fontaine and Eze tie at 15; Fontaine is in subgroup I and Eze in subgroup II, and subgroup I ranks ahead, so Fontaine ranks ahead notwithstanding Eze's earlier SCD. Dalton's 13.5 is above Bianchi's 13.
(c) Under the earlier rules described in the 2026 documents, Bianchi would have stood above Abbott. The old order was tenure group I, II, III; then veterans' preference subgroup AD, A, B within each tenure group; then length of service as augmented by performance credit. Bianchi was in AD and Abbott in B, so Bianchi's AD status controlled before performance or service. 2026-15665, 91 FR 49198.
(d) Bianchi may inspect the complete retention register for her competitive level, including the names of all other listed employees and their performance credit, veterans' preference augmentation, and service computation dates, and the complete retention registers for other positions that could affect the composition of her competitive level or her assignment rights. 5 CFR 351.506(b), (c), as revised.
Q2.uncertainty: The scenario assumes Eze is in the competitive service and the same competitive level; if his term appointment were in the excepted service, he would not be in the competitive service tenure group.

Q3.answer:
(a) A: Not a preference eligible. Retirement is not disability-based under 351.504(b)(1); retired pay is based on 22 years of active service, so (b)(2) does not apply; no continuous civilian employment since 1964 under (b)(3); not a disabled veteran, so (b)(4)-(5) do not apply. Points 0; subgroup B.
B: Not a preference eligible for RIF purposes. Retirement is based on length of service, not disability, so (b)(1) does not apply; retired pay is based on 21 years, so (b)(2) does not apply; (b)(3) does not apply. Although a disabled veteran and a commander (major or above equivalent), 351.504(b)(4) requires that he also meet (b)(1), (2), or (3), which he does not. Points 0; subgroup B.
C: Preference eligible under 351.504(b)(1)(i): disability retirement for injury received in the line of duty as a direct result of armed conflict. 60% compensable disability = +5; subgroup AD.
D: Not a preference eligible. No disability; retired pay based on 24 years, so (b)(2) does not apply; no continuous civilian employment since 1964; master sergeant is below major, so (b)(4)-(5) do not apply. Points 0; subgroup B.
E: Preference eligible under 351.504(b)(2): retired pay is not based on 20 or more years of full-time active service (16 years). 10% disability is below 30%, so +3; subgroup A.
(b) Employee A: He is a retired member covered by 351.504(b) but is not a preference eligible. Under 351.505(b)(2)(i) he receives credit only for active service during a war or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign or expedition badge was authorized: 2 years. SCD = September 7, 2010 - 2 years = September 7, 2008. Employee C: He is a preference eligible under 351.504(b), so under 351.505(b)(2)(ii) he receives credit for total active service: 14 years. SCD = September 7, 2010 - 14 years = September 7, 1996.
(c) The veterans' preference subgroups (AD, A, B) do not independently order employees on the retention register. They determine the points added to performance credit: AD = 5, A = 3, B = 0 (351.504(a)). The augmented performance credit is the primary ranking factor within the tenure group; ties are broken by tenure subgroup and then by service computation date, not by veterans' preference subgroup (351.501(b)-(c)). The subgroup is an identifier shown on the register and in the RIF notice (351.802(a)(2)).
Q3.uncertainty: The result for Employee B follows the text of 351.504(b), even though it produces no preference for a 40% disabled retired commander; the regulation makes retired-member preference conditional on meeting (b)(1), (2), or (3).

Q4.answer:
(a) The four-year period before the September 3, 2026 notices runs from September 3, 2022 to September 3, 2026. All five ratings are within it. The three most recent are August 10, 2026 (Level 5 = 7), November 14, 2025 (Level 3 = 3), and November 15, 2024 (Level 3 = 3). Performance credit = 7 + 3 + 3 = 13.
(b) A cutoff 45 days before September 3, 2026 is July 20, 2026. The four-year period before the cutoff runs from July 20, 2022. The August 10, 2026 rating is after the cutoff and is excluded. The three most recent before the cutoff are November 14, 2025 (Level 3 = 3), November 15, 2024 (Level 3 = 3), and November 20, 2023 (Level 4 = 5). Performance credit = 3 + 3 + 5 = 11.
(c) No. To be used, a rating of record must have been issued with all reviews and signatures and must also be on record, meaning available for use by the office responsible for establishing retention registers, by the applicable cutoff. The July 15, 2026 rating was not entered until August 15, 2026, after the July 20, 2026 cutoff, so it cannot be used. 5 CFR 351.503(c)(2)-(3).
(d) The four-year period before the September 3, 2026 notices begins September 3, 2022. The August 15, 2022 Level 5 rating is outside it. She has two actual ratings: November 15, 2024 (Level 4 = 5) and November 14, 2025 (Level 3 = 3). Proxy = (5 + 3) / 2 = 4. Performance credit = 5 + 3 + 4 = 12.
(e) Under 351.503(f)(1), an employee with no rating of record during the four-year period receives performance credit based on the modal rating for the summary-level pattern applicable to the official position. The final rule describes the modal rating as the most common rating assigned to other employees (91 FR 49193). In a five-level pattern the modal rating is ordinarily Level 3, which would produce 3 x 3 = 9 points. The actual modal rating must be determined from the agency's appraisal data and the definition of modal rating in 5 CFR 351.203, which is not printed in the 2026 documents.
Q4.uncertainty: The definition of modal rating in 5 CFR 351.203 is not printed in the Federal Register documents, so the value cannot be verified from these documents alone; the answer of 9 assumes the ordinary five-level modal rating is Level 3.

Q5.answer:
(a)(i) Notice August 28, 2026; effective October 27, 2026. Because the notice was issued before September 2, 2026, the earlier rules apply (2026-15665 DATES, 91 FR 49178). Under the earlier rules described in the 2026 documents, employees are ranked by tenure group, then veterans' preference subgroup, then years of service as augmented by performance credit. Both Lee and Park are career, tenure group I, and both are in veterans' preference subgroup B. Old performance credit: Level 5 = 20 years, Level 4 = 16 years, Level 3 = 12 years per rating; the three values are added and divided by 3, rounded up. Lee: (12 + 12 + 12) / 3 = 12 years; adjusted SCD = March 2, 1998 - 12 years = March 2, 1986. Park: (20 + 20 + 20) / 3 = 20 years; adjusted SCD = July 8, 2019 - 20 years = July 8, 1999. Lee's earlier adjusted SCD ranks him higher, so Park is released.
(ii) Notice September 2, 2026. The amended rules apply because the notice was issued on or after September 2, 2026. Lee: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. Park: 7 + 7 + 7 = 21. Park ranks higher, so Lee is released.
(iii) Notice September 3, 2026. The amended rules apply. Same arithmetic: Lee 9, Park 21; Lee is released.
(b) No. Under 5 CFR 351.805(b), an amended notice issued solely to state a later effective date is not a new specific RIF notice for purposes of 351.507 and does not require the agency to redetermine or recalculate retention standing. Retention standing is fixed as of the date the employee received the specific RIF notice, September 3, 2026 (351.507(a)). Lee's October 15 rating was received after the notice date and is not used; ratings are the three most recent received during the four-year period before issuance of the notices (351.503(c)(1)).
(c) The three events are: which version of the rules applies is fixed by the date the agency issues the specific RIF notice: before September 2, 2026, earlier rules; on or after, amended rules (2026-15665 DATES, 91 FR 49178; 91 FR 49206-49207). The end of the four-year period for ratings is the date the agency issues RIF notices or, if a cutoff date is established, the cutoff date (351.503(c)(1), (c)(2), (c)(4)(i)). Tenure subgroup and retention standing are fixed as of the date the employee receives a specific RIF notice (351.502(a)(2), (a)(3), (b)(2), (b)(3); 351.507(a)-(b).
Q5.uncertainty: The earlier rules themselves are not printed in the Federal Register; their operation is taken from OPM's descriptions in 2026-04377 and 2026-15665.

Q6.answer:
(a) Jordan has assignment rights to positions 1, 2, and 3: the GS-12 held by Ellis, the GS-11 held by Frank, and the GS-10 held by Gale. Each is held by an employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group and is within three grades below his GS-13 position in a one-grade interval progression; all are full-time and in the same competitive area. The agency must offer the position requiring no reduction or the least possible reduction in representative rate: position 1, the GS-12 held by Ellis. Positions 2 and 3 are available only if a higher position is unavailable. Position 4 (GS-9, Hana) is four grades below GS-13 and outside the three-grade limit. Position 5 (GS-12, Ito) is held by an employee with higher retention standing and is unavailable. Position 6 (GS-12, Kim) is part-time, and the offered position must have the same type of work schedule as Jordan's full-time position. Position 7 (GS-12, Lund) is in a different competitive area.
(b) If Jordan is a preference eligible with a compensable service-connected disability of 30 percent or more, the grade limit becomes five grades below GS-13 under 351.701(b)(2), so the GS-9 position held by Hana also becomes within reach. The agency must still offer the GS-12 position held by Ellis, because that requires the least reduction in representative rate.
(c) If Jordan's current annual rating of record is Level 1, he has no assignment rights at all. 5 CFR 351.701(a) requires a current annual performance rating of record of Level 2 (minimally satisfactory) or equivalent, or higher, as a condition of assignment rights. He would be separated, subject to any other applicable protection.
(d) If Jordan and all seven position holders are in the excepted service, there are no mandatory assignment rights. Under 5 CFR 351.705(a), an agency may, in its discretion, adopt provisions giving competing excepted service employees assignment rights on the same basis as competitive service employees under 351.701, but it is not required to do so. The result depends on whether the agency has adopted such a policy.
(e) The old handbook reflects rules the 2026 final rule eliminated. The former 351.701(d) restriction on employees with a current annual rating of Level 2 obtaining assignment to positions held by employees with a higher performance rating was eliminated; OPM explained that with the new performance-based ranking it is no longer necessary (91 FR 49204). The separate concepts of bumping and retreating were replaced by a single assignment-right rule: a released employee may be assigned to a position held by another employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group, within the grade limits, for which the employee is qualified (91 FR 49203-49204; executive summary at 91 FR 49178-49179). A Level 2 employee therefore is not categorically barred from assignment, and there is no separate bump/retreat analysis.
Q6.uncertainty: Positions 2 and 3 are described as lower-standing, but the scenario does not give their representative rates; the rule directs the agency to the position with the least possible reduction in representative rate, and the GS-12 is the least reduction among positions within reach.

Q7.answer:
(a) The Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB) hears her appeal. The OPM RIF appeals rule, 2026-15666, applies only to a RIF action for which the agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026 (91 FR 49230, DATES; preamble at 91 FR 49247). Morgan's notice was issued August 31, 2026, so OPM's new appeal process does not apply. MSPB's rule, 2026-16456, removes 5 CFR 1201.3(a)(6) effective September 2, 2026, but its DATES and Background state that MSPB will continue to adjudicate RIF appeals relating to agency actions taken before the effective date of OPM's rulemakings and will accept cases where the agency's RIF notice was issued before that date (91 FR 51997). The 2026 documents bearing on the answer are 2026-15666 (OPM's notice-date applicability rule) and 2026-16456 (MSPB's retained jurisdiction); 2026-15665 also bears on the RIF itself because the pre-September 2, 2026 notice means the earlier RIF regulations apply.
(b) OPM hears the appeal under 2026-15666, because the specific RIF notice was issued October 19, 2026. Morgan must file through the electronic filing system identified on OPM's website; e-mail or postal mail is not accepted absent a showing of good cause and OPM approval. 5 CFR 351.902(a). The deadline is 30 calendar days from the effective date of the action, filed by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the 30th calendar day after the effective date. 5 CFR 351.902(b). Counting: the effective date is Friday, December 18, 2026; the first day counted is December 19, 2026. December 19-31 = 13 days; January 1-17, 2027 = 17 more days; the 30th day is Sunday, January 17, 2027. Because that is a Sunday, the period extends to the first workday after; Monday, January 18, 2027 is the Martin Luther King, Jr. Day Federal holiday, so the last day is Tuesday, January 19, 2027, by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time. 5 CFR 351.902(b)(1).
(c) Morgan must prove, by a preponderance of the evidence: (1) timeliness of the written appeal; (2) that OPM has jurisdiction; (3) that the agency failed to comply with an applicable statute or OPM regulation governing RIF actions under part 351; and (4) that the failure prejudiced her by causing her to be subjected to the appealed action or to lose a materially more favorable outcome under part 351. 5 CFR 351.901(b). She is not entitled to a hearing. Review is based solely on the developed written record unless OPM determines that a hearing is necessary and efficient, meaning the written record is insufficiently developed on a material fact or there is a material disputed issue of witness credibility. 5 CFR 351.905(c).
(d) The rule provides that a RIF action taken under part 351, and any matter relating to an appeal of such an action, may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or contested through grievance arbitration. 5 CFR 351.901(c)(2). The preamble states that the final rule does not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs or adjudicate particular CBA disputes; when agreements are renegotiated, the governmentwide rule will limit agencies' duty and ability to bargain for a direct RIF appeal process inconsistent with part 351, and questions about particular existing agreement provisions, negotiability, or unfair-labor-practice allegations remain for resolution under chapter 71. 2026-15666, 91 FR 49244-49245.
(e) No. 5 CFR 351.901(c)(4) provides that a party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under subpart I; 5 CFR 351.909(e) provides that there is no further right of appeal of a final OPM decision.
(f) Yes. 5 CFR 351.902(b)(3) permits an employee who, before the RIF appeal filing period expires, timely filed a complaint, appeal, or other matter within the independent jurisdiction of an entity identified in 351.901(c)(3), including the Office of Special Counsel, to file a RIF appeal within 30 calendar days after the date the decision on that matter becomes final and is no longer subject to further administrative review, where the decision materially affects the employee's retention standing, order of release, assignment rights, or other rights under part 351. OPM determines in its sole and exclusive discretion whether the decision materially affects her rights. The final decision was March 10, 2027; counting March 11 as day 1, the 30th day is April 9, 2027 (Friday). She must file by April 9, 2027, by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time under 351.902(b).
(g) The provision that decides between (a) and (b) is the DATES paragraph of OPM's RIF appeals final rule, 2026-15666, 91 FR 49230: This final rule applies only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026. The preamble at 91 FR 49247 explains that this applicability provision is stated in the preamble and that the regulatory text does not include a separate applicability note in 351.901.
Q7.uncertainty: 2026-16456 is internally inconsistent about which pre-effective-date RIF appeals MSPB will continue to hear: its DATES and Background use the date the agency action was taken or the RIF notice was issued, while its section III uses the RIF effective date. In Morgan's (a) situation the notice was issued before September 2, 2026 but the separation takes effect October 30, 2026; the Background language supports MSPB jurisdiction, while section III's RIF effective date language would suggest otherwise. See Q14.

Q8.answer:
(a) Version in force today (before November 18, 2026). The current 5 CFR 351.806 is not printed in full in the 2026 Federal Register documents. OPM describes it in the proposed rule as directing agencies to keep a RIF-affected employee in duty status during the RIF notice period when possible. 2026-13073, 91 FR 39034, 39036. The current provision thus states a duty-status expectation but does not itself authorize administrative leave.
Version adopted but not yet in force. 2026-21320, 91 FR 65924, effective November 18, 2026, revises 5 CFR 351.806 to read: (a) General: Under ordinary circumstances, an employee will remain in a duty status during the notice period. (b) Administrative leave: Nothing in this section precludes an agency from placing an employee on administrative leave for all or part of the notice period when the agency determines that such leave is appropriate and the use of administrative leave is consistent with part 630, subpart N, of this chapter. (c) Emergency lack of work or funds: the agency may place the employee on annual leave with or without consent, on leave without pay with consent, or in a nonpay status without consent. 91 FR 65939.
(b) Under the adopted text and its companion leave provision, employee consent is not required. The rule uses placing an employee on administrative leave, and 5 CFR 630.1403(c)(10) authorizes administrative leave for employees subject to an involuntary RIF separation during the period between receipt of the RIF notice and the RIF separation when the agency determines it is in the Government's best interests. The preamble explains that the change from grant to provide throughout subpart N encompasses uses with or without the employee's consent, and that agency discretion is sole and exclusive and may not be limited by any agreement. 91 FR 65936. As to duration, 351.806(b) limits the leave to all or part of the notice period, and 630.1403(c)(10) limits it to the period between receipt of the notice and separation. The general subpart N principle is that administrative leave is ordinarily for not more than one workday, but longer periods may be approved in the circumstances listed in 630.1403(c) or when otherwise appropriate, 630.1403(a)(3). The 12-week workforce-realignment limit described in the preamble is stated for the uses in 630.1403(c)(9) and (c)(11), not for the RIF-notice use in (c)(10).
(c) Before the adopted text takes effect, OPM says administrative leave during a RIF notice period was allowed by OPM policy guidance, specifically section D.1.b of the Template for Agency Administrative Leave Policies (CPM 2025-12, July 30, 2025), which provided that an authorized agency official may provide administrative leave between an employee's receipt of a notice of involuntary separation and the effective date of that separation. 2026-21320, 91 FR 65926.
(d) No. OPM states that new 630.1403(c)(10) and revised 351.806 address only whether an employee may be placed in a paid, non-duty status during a RIF notice period; they do not alter the substantive or procedural requirements governing RIF, which continue to apply in full, and nothing in the rule authorizes an agency to bypass RIF competition, retention registers, or appeal rights. 91 FR 65926. Retention standing remains fixed as of the date the employee receives the specific RIF notice (5 CFR 351.507), and notice and appeal rights are unchanged (5 CFR 351.802; 2026-15666).
Q8.uncertainty: The full text of 5 CFR 351.806 as it applies today is not printed in the 2026 documents; only OPM's description (when possible) is available. The preamble's 12-week workforce-realignment limit is stated for 630.1403(c)(9) and (c)(11) and is not repeated for (c)(10), so whether it could apply by policy to RIF-notice leave is not established by the regulatory text.

Q9.answer:
Step 1: Does not comply. The Tulsa Field Office was established as a separate competitive area on August 17, 2026, less than 90 days before the October 13, 2026 notices. Under 5 CFR 351.402(c), the agency was required to submit a description of the competitive area and a written statement explaining the bona fide organizational basis to OPM for approval in advance of the RIF. Nothing was sent to OPM. The agency head's designee's approval is not enough; OPM approval was required.
Step 2: In order. A career-conditional employee serving an initial probationary period is not a competing employee under 5 CFR 351.202(d)(2)(ii), and the agency may retain such an employee while releasing a competing employee under 351.202(d)(3).
Step 3: Does not comply. A career employee with career tenure who is serving only a supervisory probationary period is not serving an initial probationary period. 5 CFR 351.203 defines initial probationary period to exclude the probationary period on initial appointment to a supervisory or managerial position. She is in competitive service tenure subgroup I under 351.502(a)(2) and must be included on the retention register and ranked. The preamble confirms this at 91 FR 49191.
Step 4: Does not comply. The cutoff date is 30 days before October 13, 2026 = September 13, 2026. A rating of record received and put on record on October 2, 2026 is after the cutoff and cannot be used. 5 CFR 351.503(c)(2)-(3). A rating cannot be used merely because it raises an employee's score; the cutoff and on-record requirements apply uniformly.
Step 5: Does not comply. For two actual ratings, the missing rating is scored as the average of the two actual values: (7 + 5) / 2 = 6. Quist's performance credit is 7 + 5 + 6 = 18, not 15.
Step 6: Does not comply. Additional performance points for a quality step increase are permitted only in the limited circumstances of 5 CFR 351.503(d) (single rating pattern where the highest summary level is Level 3) or (e) (multiple rating patterns and transmutation). All employees here are rated under one five-level pattern, so the blanket 2-point addition is not authorized.
Step 7: In order. When employees are tied on performance credit as augmented by veterans' preference, are in the same tenure subgroup, and have identical service computation dates, 5 CFR 351.601(c) permits the agency to select any tied employee for release.
Step 8: Does not comply. 5 CFR 351.602(a) prohibits releasing a competing employee from a competitive level while retaining in that level an employee with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion. Mr. Reyes's temporary promotion ends in March 2027; he may not be retained while a competing employee is released.
Step 9: In order. 5 CFR 351.702(a)(4)(v) provides that an assessment is not required if, during the five-year period ending on the date the employee receives the specific RIF notice, the employee occupied the same position (or one at the same grade/pay level with substantially the same duties, series, qualifications, and conditions) and received a rating of record of Level 3 or higher for performance of those duties. Silva held the same position until 2023 and received a Level 4 rating in 2022, within the five years before October 13, 2026.
Step 10: Does not comply. 5 CFR 351.702(a)(4)(iii) prohibits an assessment that consists solely of, or principally relies on, an automated self-assessment. An online self-rating questionnaire scored automatically is precisely such an assessment.
Step 11: Does not comply. The undue-interruption exception under 5 CFR 351.608(b) is limited to 90 days, and 351.608(a)(3) provides that each exception stands alone and may not be sequenced or stacked with another exception. The agency may apply the single exception that provides the longest period of retention (up to 90 days), but it may not add a further 60 days under 351.608(g) after the first 60 days.
Step 12: Does not comply. The RIF notices were issued October 13, 2026, on or after September 2, 2026, so RIF appeals go to OPM, not MSPB. The notice must state the employee's right to appeal to OPM, the time limit under 5 CFR 351.902(b), and the electronic filing system identified on OPM's website. 5 CFR 351.802(a)(6), as revised by 2026-15666; 2026-16456 removed MSPB's RIF appeal jurisdiction.
Q9.uncertainty: For step 9, the scenario states Silva held the same position until 2023; the exception also requires substantially the same duties, series, qualifications, and conditions of employment, which the scenario does not detail. For step 11, the agency could potentially use a different single exception with a longer authorized period, but it may not stack the 60-day undue-interruption and 60-day general temporary exceptions.

Q10.answer:
(a) On September 10, 2026, 5 CFR 330.602's definition of displaced, paragraph (1), contained only the introductory text: A current competitive service employee in the competitive service tenure group at grade GS-15 (or equivalent) or below (or another qualifying competitive service appointment, as determined by OPM) who:. It did not contain subparagraphs (i) and (ii), because amendatory instruction 11 of 2026-15665 set out only the introductory text and thereby inadvertently removed them. 2026-18800, 91 FR 58363.
(b) Changed by 2026-18800, 91 FR 58363-58364, published and effective September 15, 2026, restoring 330.602(1)(i) and (ii). OPM invoked good cause under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B), finding no substantive change because the correction restores pre-September 2, 2026 text that OPM did not propose to remove and the final rule did not discuss removing, and under 553(d)(3) made it effective on publication. OPM characterized it as correcting an inadvertent removal and as non-substantive.
(c) After the correction, paragraph (1)(i) covers an employee who received a RIF separation notice and has not declined an offer under part 351, subpart G, of a position with the same type of work schedule and a representative rate at least as high as that of the position from which the employee will be separated. If Nadia is offered a full-time position with a lower representative rate and declines, the declined offer does not meet the at-least-as-high condition, so she remains displaced under (1)(i). If the offered position had the same representative rate and same type of work schedule, her declination would mean she is not displaced under (1)(i).
Q10.uncertainty: The full pre-September 2 text is not otherwise printed, but 2026-18800 quotes the restored paragraphs.

Q11.answer:
Comparing the part 351 regulatory text of 2026-04377, 91 FR 10926-10934, with 2026-15665, 91 FR 49218-49226 (as corrected by 2026-17335), the real differences are:
1. 351.202(d) heading/framing: proposed said the provisions of this part do not apply to the listed categories; final says an employee holding one of the appointments is not a competing employee for RIF purposes.
2. 351.202(d)(1)(ii), (2)(i), (2)(ii): proposed included as of the date the agency issues a specific RIF notice; final omits those date clauses.

Q12.answer:
(a) GS-13 retention register. All are in the competitive service tenure group; the register is built under 5 CFR 351.501-351.504 as revised. Quinn is not on the register: she is a career-conditional employee serving the initial probationary period, excluded as a competing employee by 351.202(d)(2)(ii) and retainable under 351.202(d)(3). The other six:
Alvarez: 7 + 7 + 5 = 19; no preference = 0; total 19; subgroup I.
Brandt: 3 + 5 + 0 = 8; 30%+ disability = +5 (AD); total 13; subgroup I.
Chen: ratings on September 30, 2022, November 14, 2024, November 13, 2025. The four-year period before October 5, 2026 begins October 5, 2022, so the September 30, 2022 rating is outside. She has two actual ratings: 5 + 3 = 8; proxy = 4; credit = 5 + 3 + 4 = 12; no preference = 0; total 12; subgroup I.
Dube: 5 + 5 = 10; preference eligible no disability = +3; total 13; subgroup II (career-conditional, completed initial probation, not career).
Estrada: ratings November 15, 2023 (5), November 14, 2024 (3), November 13, 2025 (5), October 20, 2026 (5). The October 20, 2026 rating is after the October 5, 2026 notice date and is not used. Three most recent in the period: November 13, 2025 = 5; November 14, 2024 = 3; November 15, 2023 = 5. Credit = 5 + 3 + 5 = 13; preference eligible no disability = +3; total 16; subgroup I.
Farouk: one rating November 14, 2024, Level 3 = 3 x 3 = 9; no preference = 0; total 9; subgroup I. He is on the register because he was restored under part 353; he is a restoration protected employee only if still within the 353.209(b) protection period, which the scenario does not establish.
Order of retention: Alvarez (19), Estrada (16), Brandt (13), Dube (13), Chen (12), Farouk (9). Brandt and Dube tie at 13; Brandt is in subgroup I and Dube in subgroup II, so Brandt ranks ahead under 351.501(c).
(b) The three released are Farouk, Chen, and Dube. Farouk is last (9). Chen is next (12). Dube is tied with Brandt at 13 but is lower because he is in tenure subgroup II while Brandt is in subgroup I; Dube is therefore the third release. If Farouk were a restoration protected employee within the 353.209(b) period, 351.606(a) would require the agency to release another competing employee instead if one may be released.
(c) Offers are made under 351.701 to positions in the same competitive area, with the same type of work schedule, within three grades below the released employee's position in the released employee's one-grade interval progression, held by an employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group for which the employee is qualified. The GS-12, GS-11, GS-10, and GS-9 positions are each one grade apart and all within three grades of GS-13. Gomez (GS-12) has 19 (5+5+5=15 plus 0? No: Gomez Level 5,4,4 = 7+5+5 = 17), Hill (GS-11) has 5+3+3=11 plus 3 = 14, Jones (GS-10) has 5+5+5=15, Ikeda (GS-9) has 3+3+3=9. Each is in a separate competitive level of one, so each has a retention standing. Because all three released employees are career/competitive service, the agency must offer the position requiring no reduction or the least possible reduction in representative rate.
For Dube (13): Gomez 17 is higher, so not available; Hill 14 is higher, so not available; Jones 15 is higher, so not available; Ikeda 9 is lower, so the GS-9 is available. Dube must be offered the GS-9 held by Ikeda.
For Chen (12): Gomez 17 higher; Hill 14 higher; Jones 15 higher; Ikeda 9 lower. Chen must be offered the GS-9 held by Ikeda.
For Farouk (9): all four holders have higher standing (Gomez 17, Hill 14, Jones 15, Ikeda 9 tie? Ikeda has 9 too; Farouk 9 and Ikeda 9 are tied. The scenario says each holder is qualified only for the position they hold; the assignment right requires lower retention standing, and a tie is not lower. If Farouk and Ikeda tie at 9, Ikeda is not lower, so no position is available; if a tie is resolved in Farouk's favor, the GS-9 could be available. The documents do not address a tie between a released employee and a position holder for assignment-right purposes.) Assuming no lower-standing position is available, Farouk has no assignment right and is separated.
But the question asks which position must be offered for each released employee and why not the others. Because Gomez, Hill, Jones, and Ikeda each occupy a competitive level of one, and the released employees are from the GS-13 level, the assignment-right comparison is to the holder's retention standing. Dube and Chen can only reach Ikeda; Farouk cannot reach any if Ikeda ties at 9.
(d) If every offer is accepted: Dube and Chen are assigned to the GS-9 position held by Ikeda. Only one can actually be placed in that position; the other would displace Ikeda and then the displaced employee's own rights would have to be considered. The documents do not resolve how two released employees with rights to the same single position are sequenced. The agency has three positions to abolish; Farouk is separated; one of Dube or Chen is placed in the GS-9; the other must be separated if no other position is available. Thus, Farouk and one of Dube or Chen are separated, and the remaining released employee is assigned to the GS-9.
Q12.uncertainty: The scenario does not give the representative rates of the four lower positions or state whether the agency has adopted a policy for excepted service assignment; all are stated to be qualified. The tie between Farouk and Ikeda at 9 is not resolved by the text, and the sequencing of two employees with rights to the same single position is not addressed in the documents.

Q13.answer:
Preamble statements in 2026-15665 that differ from the same document's amendatory instructions or regulatory text:
1. Erosion-of-duties provision and trigger. The preamble says OPM is modifying Sec. 351.201(a)(2) to remove erosion-of-duties reclassifications from RIF procedures if the action would take effect after a RIF announcement and the RIF would take effect within 180 days (91 FR 49190). The actual amendment to 351.201(a)(2) contains no erosion-of-duties clause (91 FR 49218); the operative provision is 351.202(c)(3), which bars the reclassification between formal announcement and completion of the RIF where it would adversely affect retention standing (91 FR 49218). The trigger is adverse effect, not a 180-day RIF effective date, and the paragraph is 351.202(c)(3), not 351.201(a)(2). Another passage at 91 FR 49190-49191 states the adverse-effect point correctly.
2. Paragraph of 353.301. The preamble says OPM is revising Sec. 353.301(b) (91 FR 49206). The amendatory instruction and text revise Sec. 353.301(a) (91 FR 49226-49227). Another passage at 91 FR 49206 correctly says 353.301(a).
3. Composition of competitive service tenure subgroup II. The preamble says subgroup II excludes employees serving an initial probationary period or a temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less (91 FR 49196-49197). The regulatory text of 351.502(a)(3) excludes only a temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of part 316 (91 FR 49220); it does not exclude term appointments. An earlier passage at 91 FR 49190-49191 correctly describes the temporary appointment exclusion.
4. Period and condition for 351.503(d). The preamble says new 351.503(d) describes employees covered under the same rating pattern during the 4-year period before the RIF notice or cutoff date (91 FR 49197). The regulatory text of 351.503(d) contains no 4-year or cutoff condition; it applies if all competing employees in the competitive area have ratings under a single pattern (91 FR 49221).
5. Paragraph for modified notice when a competitive area is abolished. The preamble says the introductory phrase in 351.802(a) accounts for modified notices allowed under Sec. 351.605(b) (91 FR 49205). The modified notice provision is 351.605(c); 351.605(b) is the abolishment rule (91 FR 49223). Another passage at 91 FR 49203 correctly identifies 351.605(c).
Q13.uncertainty: The preamble is lengthy; I list only statements about what the final rule provides that conflict with the final regulatory text or amendatory instructions. Other differences may exist in portions not examined.

Q14.answer:
(i) Preamble statements in OPM's appeals rule that differ from its regulatory text as published or corrected:
- The preamble says 351.901(c)(1) makes the procedures in part 351 the sole and exclusive means (91 FR 49247; see also 91 FR 49253). The corrected regulatory text says the procedures in this subpart are (5 CFR 351.901(c)(1), 91 FR 49263, corrected at 91 FR 54796).
- The preamble says OPM or the responsible agency may disallow a representative who is an employee of the responsible agency or OPM (91 FR 49250; see also 91 FR 49231). The corrected text says OPM or the agency whose action is under appeal and an employee of that agency or OPM (351.904(c), 91 FR 49265, corrected at 91 FR 54796).
- The preamble says paragraph (f) protects protected personnel information (91 FR 49253). The corrected text says protected personal information (351.909(f), 91 FR 49267, corrected at 91 FR 54796).
- The preamble describes the collateral-matter entity as identified in Sec. 351.901(c) (91 FR 49249). The corrected text says Sec. 351.901(c)(3) (351.902(b)(3), 91 FR 49264, corrected at 91 FR 54796).
(ii) Changes from the proposed appeals rule to the final appeals rule not acknowledged in the summary at 91 FR 49230-49232:
- The proposed rule required the RIF notice to state the appeal right to OPM and that the agency must also comply with Sec. 1201.21 (2026-02576, 91 FR 5874). The final rule deletes that sentence and substitutes the time limit and electronic filing system (2026-15666, 91 FR 49263). The summary mentions the added filing detail but not the deletion of the MSPB-specific 1201.21 requirement (discussed at 91 FR 49247-49248).
- The proposed 351.901(c) preserved matters within the jurisdiction of the EEOC, the Federal Labor Relations Authority, an Inspector General, MSPB, DOL VETS, and OSC (91 FR 5875). The final 351.901(c)(3) omits the FLRA and lists EEOC, an Inspector General, MSPB, DOL VETS, and OSC (91 FR 49264). The summary does not acknowledge the FLRA's removal.
- The proposed 351.903(b) required the agency response within 30 calendar days of the initial appeal (91 FR 5875). The final rule requires it within 30 calendar days after service of the initial appeal, and says the 30 days begins upon service (91 FR 49264). The summary does not mention this change in trigger.
- The proposed 351.906(b) said OPM shall impose the listed consequences (91 FR 5876). The final rule says OPM may impose them, and adds 351.906(c) requiring proportionality and a causal relationship (91 FR 49266). The summary does not mention these changes.
- The proposed 351.902(c)(2) barred filing or access unless registered as an e-filer (91 FR 5875). The final rule adds or exempted under paragraph (c)(7) for good cause (91 FR 49264). The summary's e-filing discussion does not mention this addition.
(iii) Inconsistencies about which RIF appeals MSPB will still hear: 2026-16456 uses three different triggers. Its DATES say MSPB will not apply the rule to cases relating to agency actions taken before the effective date of OPM's rulemakings (91 FR 51997). Its Background says MSPB will accept cases where the agency's RIF notice was issued before the rule's effective date (91 FR 51997). Its section III says MSPB will adjudicate RIF appeals received after September 2, 2026 in which the RIF effective date preceded September 2, 2026 (91 FR 51998). OPM's rule uses a fourth formulation: it applies only where the agency issues the specific RIF notice on or after September 2, 2026 (2026-15666, 91 FR 49230). Thus, for a RIF with a notice issued before September 2, 2026 but an effective date after that date, MSPB's Background says MSPB will hear it, MSPB's section III says it will not, and OPM's notice-based rule says OPM does not hear it.
Q14.uncertainty: The summary of changes is not exhaustive; the items in (ii) are changes verified in the regulatory text that the summary does not mention. The MSPB inconsistency is unresolved; the most defensible reading for pre-September 2 notices is that MSPB retains jurisdiction, because that is the trigger in OPM's rule and MSPB's Background, but MSPB's section III uses a different trigger.
